test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 16 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by four conclusions numbered I, II, III and IV. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements

**Statements:**

1. Some pants are coats.

2. All coats are red.

3. All red are shirts.

**Conclusions:**

I. All pants are shirts.

Il. All coats are shirts.

IIl. Some red are coats.

IV. Some shirts are pants.

options.text: Only conclusions II, III and IV follow
Only conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusions I, III and IV follow

solution:
**Statement:**

1. Some pants are coats.

2. All coats are red.

3. All red are shirts.

**Venn Diagram:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b72304cb7da591851eec0b364f56254f3a23bcb67799d4f25318b00932de117.png] 

Conclusions:

I. All pants are shirts. → False (Some pants are coats and all coats are shirts but we do NOT have a direct relation between pants and shirts so we can't conclude that all pants are shirts)

Il. All coats are shirts. → True (Since we have All coats are red and All red are shirts, so we can say that All coats are shirts)

IIl. Some red are coats. → True (Since All coats are red so we can say that Some red are coats)

IV. Some shirts are pants. → True (Since we have All coats are shirts and some pants are coats so we can say that Some shirts are pants)

According to the diagram, conclusions II, III, and IV follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1)**.
